newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile-U.S. air traffic treaty goes into effect.
newsitem.headline: Chile-U.S. air traffic treaty goes into effect.

text.p: Chile officially put into effect Thursday an air traffic treaty with the United States signed in March and which allows up to 35 flights a week between the two countries.
Contained in a decree, the treaty was signed by President Eduardo Frei and published in the official gazette.

The treaty allows carriers to fly 21 flights a week without stopovers all year round, plus seven more flights between December 15 and February 28, and June 15 and August 15, and seven further flights with at least one stopover.

The treaty also sets the dates and terms under which private airlines designated by each country may fly between U.S. and Chilean cities, and also the type of airline they may use. The agreement will be in effect until December 31, 1998.
